title: ～はずがない — “there's no way ～”
summary: はずがない is the negative of はず: the speaker strongly believes that something cannot possibly be true. It uses the same connections as はずだ.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞の普通形 ＋ はずがない
patterns.gloss: つく → つくはずがない / 間違える → 間違えるはずがない

patterns.form: 名詞＋の／な形容詞＋な ＋ はずがない
patterns.gloss: 本物のはずがない / 簡単なはずがない

body.p: It replaces the だ of はずだ with がない, literally “there is no reason for it to be so.” The result is a strong negative guess. You can also say はずはない.
Use it when you cannot believe what someone says or when you want to rule something out on solid grounds: 彼がうそをつくはずがありません. The polite form is はずがありません.
It is very firm and can sound rude to someone who has just given their opinion. It also differs slightly from ～ないはずだ (“should not ～”): はずがない denies the very possibility.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）がうそをつくはずがありません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga uso o tsuku hazu ga arimasen.
examples.tr: There's no way he would lie.

examples.ja: こんなに簡単（かんたん）な問題（もんだい）を間違（まちが）えるはずがない。
examples.romaji: Konna ni kantan na mondai o machigaeru hazu ga nai.
examples.tr: There's no way I'd get such an easy question wrong.

examples.ja: やさしい友（とも）だちが、そんなことを言（い）うはずがない。
examples.romaji: Yasashii tomodachi ga, sonna koto o iu hazu ga nai.
examples.tr: There's no way such a kind friend would say something like that.

pitfalls: Nouns take の and na-adjectives take な: 本物のはずがない, 簡単なはずがない.
It is not for denying your own will. 行かないはずがない means “there is no way he would not go.”
